critical_findings: The current recovery sbatch and runner contain malformed doubled-dollar shell parameter expansions. Bash expands the doubled dollar to the process id before the brace text.
The recovery CI did not independently detect this bug. Its shell-boundary assertion encoded the malformed spelling as the expected string, so implementation and validator shared the same defect.
This is direct evidence that current CPU/static qualification can be self-referential: the same authoring path can reproduce the same mistaken assumption in both implementation and test.

The current T2 curriculum is a synthetic operator-unit-test grammar, not a realistic public N0 relation/evidence distribution. T1 field text is deliberately opaque neutral evidence record hashes; T2 query text is generated from small operation/relation/role phrase banks.
The T2 DEV split uses disjoint phrase banks but the same family-specific grammar. Operation/control labels are often recoverable from highly available lexical cues.

CPU deterministic/oracle passes and GPU learned-model runs are not the same experiment. Many historical CPU passes prove interface representability or plumbing, while GPU is the first point where learned predictions, the exact container/runtime, and the full evaluator interact.
The history contains both genuine GPU model failures and non-model harness/runtime failures. They must not be collapsed into one category.
QSRE itself is not rejected by this audit. T1 produced a genuine P100 DEV-contract pass. T2 has not yet produced a valid PASS or FAIL model result.
